title: Quandela Expands International Photonic Footprint with Deployment Alliance in Qatar and Foundry MoU in Taiwan - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
European photonic quantum computing developer Quandela has signed two international collaboration agreements aimed at advancing both sovereign quantum infrastructure in the Middle East and photonic component industrialization in Asia. Announced at Mobile World Congress 26 Doha and Hsinchu Science Park on November 12 and 13, 2026, the initiatives pair Quandela’s quantum-dot photonic architectures with regional data center and semiconductor manufacturing partners.

In Qatar, Quandela entered a tripartite partnership with publicly listed technology group Mekdam Holding Group Q.P.S.C. and managed IT and data center provider MEEZA QSTP-LLC to deploy cloud and on-premises photonic quantum systems across Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states. Expanding on a June 2026 agreement to establish a Quandela-Mekdam Quantum Center of Excellence in Doha, the alliance integrates Quandela’s platforms into MEEZA’s sovereign data centers to support fault-tolerant quantum computing, quantum machine learning, and workforce certification initiatives aligned with Qatar National Vision 2030.

Separately, Quandela signed a memorandum of understanding with Taiwan-based semiconductor equipment and quantum foundry supplier Hermes-Epitek Corporation to co-develop and industrialize integrated photonic quantum hardware. The initial joint R&D phase combines Quandela’s semiconductor quantum-dot single-photon sources and photonic integrated circuits with Hermes-Epitek’s superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) and cryogenic systems on a fiber-coupled testbed in Taiwan, establishing a pathway toward a subsequent joint system installation subject to definitive agreements.
